text:
Alex: quick handoff for night shift — main items below, short and actionable. primary: Jamal (overnight). secondary: Mira (backup). Priya will cover escalations for Dedicated customers until 03:00 PST.

Alex: Summary of what happened earlier (21:12 UTC): the batcher pool hit a sustained memory pressure after a slow regression in a model-serving change. This caused OOM-induced request retries and ~2% error rate for generation endpoints for ~18 minutes. No data loss. Impact: higher p99 latency, some 5xx for short window.

inc-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: "batcher-memory-spike-176900" — Severity: SEV-2 — PagerDuty alert routed to eng-oncall. Link: https://incidents.redwood.com/176900

Jamal: saw the spike at 21:10 UTC via console alerts. Logs showed repeated batcher worker restarts. Attemped mitigation: toggled batch_size cap to 32 (from 64) which stabilized memory growth but increased p50 latency ~15ms.

Mira: noted that autoscaler responded but was slow because the new scale-up path requires additional warm-up. We hit a short window where queue depth climbed and retries amplified.

Jamal: root cause (working hypothesis): a regression in the model-wrapper that changed token caching behavior + a combo of larger model pulses from a nightly evaluation job. I've reverted the model-wrapper commit on staging and started a canary rollback on prod.

Priya: customer impact check — Dedicated clusters with reserved capacity experienced throttling for ~12 minutes. Self-serve hosted customers saw increased latency and ~2% errors as Alex mentioned. I flagged the top 3 affected customers in PM portal and sent emails to account owners.

Alex: runbooks and notes: runbook used -> https://intra.redwood.com/runbooks/batcher-oom (follow steps 1-5). Canary rollback procedure -> https://intra.redwood.com/playbooks/canary-rollback. If you need the quick command we used to cap batcher size:

```
# temporarily set batch_size_limit
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \ 
  https://api.redwood.internal/configs/batcher -d '{"batch_size_limit":32}'
```

Mira: monitoring checks to follow: watch worker restarts (metric: batcher.worker_restarts), memory RSS per pod (batcher.rss), and queue depth (batcher.queue_depth). I added a dashboard pinned in #oncall-dash.

Jamal: current status: rollback canary 60% traffic -> healthy, memory stable for 24m, no new restarts. I'll hold at 60% for one more hour, then roll to 100% if green.

inc-bot: PagerDuty: Alert acknowledged by Jamal. Escalation set: primary Jamal, secondary Mira.

Alex: coverage gaps: night coverage between 02:30–03:00 PST is thin — Priya is leaving at 03:00 and Miranda is offline. If the canary needs manual rollback after Priya signs off, either Jamal or Mira should take action. We should also notify infra team oncall (cc @infra-oncall) if memory climbs again — they own kernel-level tuning if it recurs.

Mira: follow-ups I queued: 1) add a pre-warm hook to autoscaler for model docker images; 2) add regression test for token-cache semantics in the model-wrapper CI; 3) create alert runbook with exact thresholds to avoid false positives. All in the tracker: https://tracker.redwood.com/t/PROJECT-214

Jamal: Next immediate steps for overnight: - maintain canary at 60% for next 60–90m - watch memory and restart metrics every 5m - if restarts > 3 in 15m -> rollback to known-good (rollback tag: release-2026-03-12) - escalate to Priya if customer error rate > 5% over 10m

Priya: I've prepared the customer-facing note template if we need to communicate broader impact. Saved in docs: https://intra.redwood.com/customer-comms/batcher-memory-template.md

Alex: handoff checklist for Jamal -> Mira: - confirm canary green at 23:15 UTC - if green, promote to 100% and monitor 30m - if not green, execute immediate rollback and open a follow-up incident thread with root-cause link - file postmortem draft in #postmortems with timeline and mitigation within 48h

Jamal: acknowledged. I'll post an update in this thread at 23:15 UTC and again at 00:30 UTC.

Mira: noted. I'm reachable via DM and have console access. If you need extra memory headroom quick patch: increase node pool by 2 GPUs via infra autoscaler (runbook link above).

Alex: final notes: no lasting customer data exposure, no billing changes. We should consider a short-term limit on nightly eval job concurrency until autoscaler pre-warm is in place.

Jamal: update (23:15 UTC): canary at 60% has been stable for 63m, memory flat, promoting to 100% now. Posting a short status in #general to close the loop.

Priya: confirmed promotion and will keep watch for account owner replies.

Alex: thanks everyone — jamal, mira, priya. If anything changes ping @here. I'll start the postmortem template after midnight. :white_check_mark:
